title: The Meetings & Events Event Bill: Billed Attendance, Package Charge, Service Charge and Sales Tax
content:
After a Meetings & Events function is held and the banquet captain records the attendance, the event bill is charged on the billed attendance.

## Billing rule

**Billed attendance.** The billed attendance is the greater of the guarantee and the actual attendance when the package bills on the greater of the two, and it is never less than the guarantee billing floor: the contracted attendance less the package's maximum guarantee reduction percentage, rounded up to a whole person.

**Package charge.** The package charge is the billed attendance multiplied by the package price per person.

**Service charge.** The service charge is the package's service charge percentage of food and beverage revenue, together with any minimum shortfall when the package's shortfall bears the service charge, and of room rental only when the package applies the service charge to room rental. Food and beverage revenue is the total of the contract's package charges and its additional hosted bar hour charges, before service charge and sales tax.

**Sales tax.** Sales tax at the sales tax rate recorded on the contract is charged on food and beverage revenue, on fees, on the service charge when the package's service charge bears sales tax, and on a minimum shortfall when the package's shortfall bears sales tax.

**Rounding.** Each amount is rounded to the cent.

**Status and frequency.** Event charges are posted only on a contract whose status is completed. Each component is charged once per contract.

## Billed attendance, case by case (hypothetical inputs)

| Contracted attendance | Maximum reduction | Billing floor | Guarantee | Actual attendance | Greater of guarantee and actual | Billed attendance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 10 percent | 45 | 50 | 56 | 56 | 56 |
| 50 | 10 percent | 45 | 50 | 47 | 50 | 50 |
| 100 | 10 percent | 90 | 80 | 75 | 80 | 90, held at the floor |
| 100 | 10 percent | 90 | 80 | 95 | 95 | 95 |

## Worked bill on hypothetical inputs

Inputs: a package priced at 129.00 per person with a 22 percent service charge that bears sales tax and does not apply to room rental; attendance billed on the greater of the guarantee and the actual count; a maximum guarantee reduction of 10 percent; a contract sales tax rate of 7 percent; contracted attendance 40, guarantee 38, actual attendance 41; no additional hosted bar hours, no minimum shortfall and, in this illustration, no fees outside the package.

1. Billing floor: 40 less 10 percent is 36. The greater of the guarantee of 38 and the actual 41 is 41, which is not below 36, so the billed attendance is 41.
2. Package charge: 41 multiplied by 129.00 is 5,289.00, which is also the food and beverage revenue.
3. Service charge: 22 percent of 5,289.00 is 1,163.58.
4. Sales tax: 7 percent of the food and beverage revenue of 5,289.00 is 370.23, and 7 percent of the service charge of 1,163.58 is 81.45; sales tax of 451.68 is charged.

## Basis Q&A

- **Can the event bill be posted before the function is held?** No. Event charges are posted only once the contract's status is completed.
- **Does room rental attract the service charge?** Only where the package applies the service charge to room rental.
- **Is the service charge itself taxed?** Where the package's service charge bears sales tax, yes, at the contract's rate.
- **Can the package charge be posted twice?** No; each component is charged once per contract.
